intro.en: Tengo que expresses a personal obligation; hay que expresses a general or unspecified obligation.

hay que.en: one has to, it is necessary

por qué.nota: Use two words with an accent in questions; porque means because.

bloques.texto:
**Tener que** + infinitive says who has to do it: **tengo que** estudiar.

**Hay que** + infinitive expresses a general or unspecified obligation; it does not say who has to do it: **hay que** llegar a las nueve.

Use **porque** to introduce a reason: estudio **porque** mañana hay un examen. **¿Por qué?** (two words, with an accent) asks “why.”

frases.en: Because there is an exam tomorrow.

frases.es: Hay que llegar a las nueve.
frases.en: We have to arrive at nine.
frases.nota: The Spanish phrase does not name who must arrive; the context suggests the people taking the exam.

que.en: Tener que needs que before the infinitive.

de.en: De is not the link in tengo que.

a.en: Ir a is a plan. Tener uses que.

traduccion.en: Because there is an exam tomorrow.

pregunta.en: Complete the general rule: you have to arrive at nine.

Tengo.en: Tengo que is I have to.

por qué.en: Two words, with an accent on qué, ask why.

porque.en: One word without an accent introduces a reason: because.

porqué.en: One word with an accent is a noun meaning the reason.

pregunta.en: Which sentence says I have to study?

texto.en:
**The app cannot check this part.** For the writing, please use pen and paper. For the speaking, say it out loud and, if you can, practise with a native speaker or a teacher who can correct you.

**Write (30–40 words).** Write your list of things to do this week: what you have to do and what one must do in general (hay que).

**Speak (about 30 seconds).** Explain aloud why you cannot go out tonight: give three obligations.
